column1: # Game profile of TUNIC (Switch, update 1.0.3 = v196608). Plays on the Mac

# Andrew Shouldice's game (Finji) on Unity 2020.3.36f1 IL2CPP with FMOD, SDK 14.3.0, NVN. The NSP script's provisional profile, its keys unchanged but fps_target: no rewriter cut, no host change of its own

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# every module main imports from (subsdk0 = the SDK's movie library)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap: a 5 GB block with a 4.375 GB alias region, where the game maps its memory itself
# (up to +3.02 GB of it from the title through the beach and the cliffs above it)
# a 1 GB pool, so StandardAllocator's region leaves the game room for its own (the heap check: with the hardware pool the alias region was used up to +4.26 GB of 4.38 GB)
# every shader is under Data/ (35,742) or in main (11)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game sets Unity's QualitySettings.vSyncCount to 2, which Unity hands to NVN as present interval 2, and steps by the time that really passed.
# The rewriter finds vSyncCount and Application.targetFrameRate through Unity's internal-call table (dm/tools/unity_fps.py), the host writes the target there (hle_fpslock.c).
# The speed checked at 30 and 60 by a timed walk (the same 3 s of the stick end at the same place); 120 not measured (fps_max stays 60)
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
